nodes.label: Company Account Recommendation
nodes.rationale: Store Policy 10.14 and Mirafold's branded, planned-commercial presentation favor a Company account, subject to the maintainer's unverified legal status.

nodes.label: Phase 6: Windows Proof and Microsoft Store
nodes.norm_label: phase 6: windows proof and microsoft store

nodes.label: Installed-Form Update Policy
nodes.rationale: APT, AppImage, standalone Debian, extracted tar, Windows, and future Store packages use deliberately different update mechanisms.

nodes.label: Microsoft Store Identity and Packaging Record
nodes.norm_label: microsoft store identity and packaging record

nodes.label: Desktop Pull Release Architecture
nodes.rationale: Desktop polls and verifies npm latest rather than accepting a privileged cross-repository push, avoiding a personal access token and allowing rapid Shell releases to coalesce.

nodes.label: Hosted Runner versus Human Evidence Boundary
nodes.rationale: Automation can prove silent install, runtime, process cleanup, and uninstall, but cannot observe SmartScreen, visible UI, a real agent, or human-driven updating.
nodes.norm_label: hosted runner versus human evidence boundary

nodes.label: Two-Session Windows Proof
nodes.rationale: The updater-less public v0.1.1 and lack of a higher target prevent one session from proving both candidate runtime and production updating.

nodes.label: Read-Only APT Signing Job
nodes.rationale: The archive key is isolated in a job that installs no project dependencies and has no repository-write permission.

nodes.label: APT Archive Identity and Secret Boundary
nodes.norm_label: apt archive identity and secret boundary

nodes.label: APT Distribution Channel
nodes.rationale: APT installations use a Signed-By-scoped repository identity and leave updates to APT.

nodes.label: Authenticated New Sessions
nodes.rationale: New sessions stay in the existing Desktop window because an external browser does not possess the daemon's private launch token.

nodes.label: Draft-Then-Publish Atomicity
nodes.rationale: All assets and remote metadata are verified while the release is a draft, then one final operation makes it public and latest.

nodes.label: Isolated Automated Release Writer
nodes.rationale: The only write-capable job installs no dependencies and reconstructs the exact reviewed candidate before committing, tagging, and publishing.

nodes.label: Reviewed Linux and Windows Build Job
nodes.norm_label: reviewed linux and windows build job

nodes.label: Reviewed Package and Lock Artifact
nodes.rationale: Only package.json, package-lock.json, and compact intake evidence cross the job boundary.

nodes.label: Shell Intake Owns Mirafold Version Movement
nodes.rationale: Routine Mirafold dependency version movement is reserved for Shell intake, while Dependabot may still raise security updates.
nodes.norm_label: shell intake owns mirafold version movement

nodes.label: Thin Electron Shell Boundary
nodes.rationale: Product UI, server, adapters, and protocol remain in the published mirafold package and are never vendored or patched here.

nodes.label: Child-Process Daemon Architecture
nodes.rationale: Crash isolation, event-loop isolation, and per-folder working directories require the daemon to run out of process.

nodes.label: No Renderer Bridge
nodes.rationale: No preload, IPC, or nodeIntegration preserves Mirafold's plain-browser security model.

nodes.label: Real Windows Package Smoke Check
nodes.rationale: A copied node.exe is not the packaged Electron runtime, so pull-request CI builds and smoke-checks the real Windows package.

nodes.label: main as Production Mirror
nodes.rationale: main advances only at release time so its tree and the public installers remain the same thing.

nodes.label: asar Disabled
nodes.rationale: The separate daemon cannot resolve dependencies split between app.asar and app.asar.unpacked, while asar would not materially shrink the app.

nodes.label: Linux deb, tar.gz, and AppImage Targets
nodes.rationale: The Debian package is primary, tar.gz is the no-FUSE universal fallback, and AppImage supplies the expected portable form.
nodes.norm_label: linux deb, tar.gz, and appimage targets

nodes.label: Visible Per-User NSIS Installer
nodes.rationale: Current-user scope avoids machine-wide rights, while oneClick false exposes a visible destination-selectable installer.

nodes.label: Forward-Only Bad Release Recovery
nodes.rationale: A bad release is recovered by publishing restored source under a higher Desktop version, never by replacing assets or downgrading clients.

nodes.label: Release Privilege Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Build, APT signing, provenance, and publication powers are split so no dependency-running job has write authority or the archive key.

nodes.label: Branch from next and PR into next
nodes.norm_label: branch from next and pr into next

nodes.label: Boot Loading Interface
nodes.rationale: A fast loading view prevents the short daemon-start interval from appearing as a broken blank window.

nodes.label: Self-Contained Loading Page
nodes.rationale: No fonts, scripts, or network are used so the page renders before any other application service exists.
